events.title: Matter–dark-energy equality
events.detail: Crossing of the homogeneous matter and dark-energy density fractions, located on the continuous solution.

events.title: Star formation becomes scarce
events.detail: Illustrative depletion range for gas and long-lived stellar populations; not a computed galaxy-formation history.

events.title: Dark energy becomes dynamically negligible (literal CPL extrapolation)
events.detail: With wₐ < 0 the CPL law w(a)=w₀+wₐ(1−a) grows without bound. At a = 38.7494, w = 23.7161 ≥ 1/3 and the dark-energy fraction is 2.40e-25, below the extinction threshold even when weighted by 1+3w. No supported component dilutes faster, so the fraction can never grow again; the dark energy is dropped from the background, changing H by a relative amount far below double precision. A literal extrapolation of an observational fit ansatz, not a prediction.

events.title: Long-lived normal stars fade
events.detail: Low-mass stellar lifetimes motivate this broad transition into a remnant-rich era. The plotted stellar fraction is a phenomenological proxy.

events.title: Bound systems may disperse
events.detail: Repeated gravitational encounters can eject members of bound stellar systems. Environment-dependent order-of-magnitude range.

events.title: CMB cooler than 1e+1 M☉ Hawking temperature
events.detail: Located temperature crossing: the redshifted CMB changes from hotter to colder than this ideal black hole. It is not a complete net-accretion calculation.

classification: Long-lived decelerating expansion · literal CPL extrapolation
explanation: Literal extrapolation of the observational CPL fit ansatz w(a)=w₀+wₐ(1−a) to arbitrarily large a: a mathematical consequence of the ansatz, not a prediction. With wₐ < 0, w(a) grows without bound. Once w ≥ 1/3 no supported component dilutes faster than the dark energy, so its density fraction can never grow again; it was dropped from the background once below the extinction threshold (event “Dark energy becomes dynamically negligible”). The selected model approaches a proven constant-fluid power law. Density decreases with expansion, and the future proper-time integral does not end at a finite Big Rip. Microphysical ultimate fate remains uncertain.
warnings: CPL is an observational fit ansatz, w(a)=w₀+wₐ(1−a), that diverges as a→∞. Its simulated future, including a proven dark-energy extinction or Big Rip, is a literal mathematical extrapolation of the fit, not a prediction.
Massive neutrinos are pressureless over this future-only integration. Ωr is an independently specified photons + effective massless-neutrino density. Tcmb and Neff do not silently recompute Ωr.
Stellar populations and remnant eras are phenomenological proxies; no N-body dynamics, stellar population synthesis, or exact entropy budget is computed.

diagnostics.tail: Matched constant-fluid asymptote, ρ ∝ a^(-3.0000), subdominant fraction < 10⁻⁸. Future source ratios cannot overtake the dominant term. Numeric integration ends at log10(elapsed yr)=49.32414.

metadata.solver: Dormand–Prince 5(4); log-scale-factor expansion; regular time-domain contraction; matched constant-fluid asymptotes
